question: What makes pathological waste different from normal trash?

options.A: Pathological waste is generated exclusively in hospital kitchens.
options.B: Pathological waste consists of recognizable human tissues and body parts.
options.C: Pathological waste includes only broken glass and empty medicine vials.
options.D: Pathological waste is composed strictly of administrative paper records.

explanation: Pathological waste refers to body tissues and parts. Because of what they are, they need special, respectful handling and high-heat burning.

question: A patient with an underactive thyroid gland will most likely show which sign?

options.A: Changes in energy levels and metabolism
options.B: Rapid spikes in calcium-regulating hormones
options.C: Severe trouble controlling blood sugar
options.D: Holding onto too much water with very little urine

explanation: That's right! The thyroid controls your body's engine speed, so when it slows down, the patient often feels sluggish and tired.

question: Which of these makes a research hypothesis weak and unusable?

options.A: Matching the primary research question too closely
options.B: Being based on existing nursing theory
options.C: Predicting a negative relationship between variables
options.D: Using vague terms that cannot be measured

explanation: Keep it clear! If words are too fuzzy to measure, researchers won't be able to collect real data to check if it's true.

question: What body tissue is the primary driver of a person's metabolic rate?

options.A: Bone mineral matrix
options.B: Subcutaneous water
options.C: Adipose fat tissue
options.D: Lean muscle mass

explanation: Muscle tissue burns significantly more calories at rest than fat tissue, making muscle mass the main driver of metabolism. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h4)

question: In community nursing, what does a "health need" actually mean?

options.A: The total number of hospital beds available in a district
options.B: The total population size of a specific rural village
options.C: The monthly budget allocated for primary health clinics
options.D: The gap between current health status and a desired healthy state

explanation: Spot on! Think of a health need as the distance between how healthy a community is right now and where they ought to be for good well-being.

question: Which of the following is a well-known childhood illness caused by a serious lack of protein in the diet?

options.A: Kwashiorkor
options.B: Rickets
options.C: Scurvy
options.D: Iron-deficiency anemia

explanation: You're right! Kwashiorkor happens when children don't get enough protein, often leading to swollen bellies and muscle wasting.

question: A primary school pupil comes in with round, scaly, itchy patches on their head and some hair loss in those spots. What's the most likely issue?

options.A: Tinea capitis
options.B: Herpes labialis
options.C: Scabies infestation
options.D: Cellulitis

explanation: You guessed it! Circular, scaly spots with broken hair on the scalp are the trademark signs of Tinea capitis (scalp ringworm).

question: What is the primary contribution of the seminal vesicles to semen?

options.A: Acidic waste products for disposal
options.B: Enzymes that harden the scrotal wall
options.C: Fructose-rich fluid that nourishes sperm
options.D: Aqueous fluid to cool the testicles

explanation: Seminal vesicles supply an alkaline fluid containing high levels of fructose, giving energy to the sperm cells. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is tele-nursing especially helpful for rural healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: It lets nurses care for patients without forcing long, costly travel
options.B: It eliminates all expenses related to purchasing medical equipment
options.C: It guarantees uninterrupted electricity supply in remote villages
options.D: It completely replaces the need for physical hospitals everywhere

explanation: Spot on! Many patients in rural areas spend a lot of money and time just getting to a clinic. Tele-nursing brings basic nursing advice directly to them.

question: Which cells in your body carry MHC Class I molecules on their surface?

options.A: Only mature red blood cells
options.B: Almost all nucleated cells
options.C: Only free-floating antibodies
options.D: Only uninfected skin cells

explanation: Nearly every cell with a nucleus wears MHC Class I proteins like an ID badge to show whether it is healthy or infected from within.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to mental health referrals in Nigeria?

options.A: High cost of transportation and out-of-pocket treatment expenses
options.B: Poor communication and missing feedback letters between facilities
options.C: Stigma and initial reliance on traditional or spiritual healers
options.D: Immediate availability of fully equipped psychiatric units in every rural village

explanation: Spot the trick! Fully equipped psychiatric units in every rural village definitely do not exist, making this option the false statement—and thus the correct answer.

question: What is the main goal of occupational health services?

options.A: Providing long-term retirement planning
options.B: Punishing employees who break safety rules
options.C: Reducing company expenses on worker salaries
options.D: Promoting worker well-being and preventing illness

explanation: You got this! Occupational health is all about keeping workers safe, healthy, and happy both physically and mentally. Great job!

question: Which macronutrient provides the highest number of calories per gram?

options.A: Fat
options.B: Protein
options.C: Water
options.D: Carbohydrate

explanation: Fats are the most energy-dense nutrient, supplying nine kilocalories for every single gram consumed. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h2)

question: Which antibody class shows up first at the very beginning of a brand-new infection?

options.A: IgA
options.B: IgE
options.C: IgM
options.D: IgG

explanation: Think of IgM as the first responder rushing to the scene! It is always the initial antibody type secreted when your body encounters a brand-new infection.

question: Why is a high participant dropout rate a big problem in a longitudinal study?

options.A: It automatically proves that the nursing intervention was a failure
options.B: It prevents nurses from publishing articles in international journals
options.C: The remaining participants might no longer represent the original target population
options.D: It makes the computer software run much slower during data analysis

explanation: Spot on! If a specific type of patient drops out, our final group becomes biased, which can make our conclusions inaccurate.

question: Why is land-use planning so helpful for disaster prevention?

options.A: It physically reinforces old buildings against strong winds
options.B: It provides immediate medical care to disaster survivors
options.C: It replaces the need for community disaster education
options.D: It prevents people from settling in naturally hazardous zones

explanation: Spot on! Good land-use planning keeps people and important buildings safely away from high-risk spots.

question: What major global health target was famously set by the Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Eradication of all infectious diseases by 1985
options.B: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.C: Privatization of all national health sectors
options.D: Free tertiary hospital care for every global citizen

explanation: Alma-Ata made history by rallying the world around the bold dream of 'Health for All by the Year 2000' through primary care.

question: Why do we carry out a re-audit near the end of a quality improvement cycle?

options.A: To find new reasons to query junior nursing staff members
options.B: To see if the corrective actions successfully improved care
options.C: To comply with international travel laws for nurses
options.D: To increase the amount of paperwork stored in the archive

explanation: Spot on! A re-audit helps us check whether the changes we put in place actually solved the problems we found during our first check.

question: What is the main goal of day and night hospital services?

options.A: To provide permanent housing for chronic psychiatric patients
options.B: To replace outpatient clinics entirely in rural areas
options.C: To isolate violent patients from their families permanently
options.D: To bridge the gap between full hospital admission and community life

explanation: Spot on! These services provide structured support while keeping patients connected to their families and everyday lives.

question: If a patient has a blockage in their arachnoid granulations, what process would be directly affected?

options.A: The return of cerebrospinal fluid into the venous blood stream
options.B: The initial production of cerebrospinal fluid inside the ventricles
options.C: The structural folding of the dura mater to form the falx cerebri
options.D: The tight attachment of the pia mater to the brain tissue folds

explanation: You've got this! Since arachnoid granulations act as the drainpipes for cerebrospinal fluid, a blockage stops that fluid from flowing smoothly back into the blood.

question: What is the main goal of taking medications for osteoarthritis?

options.A: To permanently cure the underlying bone disease
options.B: To stop all systemic autoimmune responses
options.C: To completely regenerate lost joint cartilage
options.D: To relieve pain and improve joint function

explanation: Well done! OA medications are meant to keep you comfortable and moving well, even though they don't cure the root condition.

question: Which emotional response is most commonly seen in patients placed in strict isolation?

options.A: Relief and joy
options.B: Confusion about medication
options.C: Aggression and anger
options.D: Loneliness and anxiety

explanation: Physical separation from family and friends combined with masked staff often leaves isolated patients feeling lonely and anxious. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h7)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to ask a patient to demonstrate how they use their inhaler?

options.A: To check if the patient is strong enough to crush the capsule
options.B: To measure how fast the patient can blow air into a balloon
options.C: To ensure the patient bought the correct brand of medication
options.D: To catch hidden errors that could prevent the medicine from working

explanation: It's easy for patients to pick up little habits over time that stop the medicine from working right. Seeing them do it live is the best way to help them correct it!

question: Why are elderly patients much more sensitive to side effects when taking multiple drugs?

options.A: They refuse to take any form of liquid medication or syrup.
options.B: Their immune systems reject synthetic chemical compounds instantly.
options.C: They always forget to take their medications at the correct hour.
options.D: Their bodies process and clear drugs more slowly due to aging organs.

explanation: As organs age, the liver and kidneys don't clear drugs as fast. This causes medications to hang around longer and build up in the body.

question: How should nurses view community challenges like poverty and lack of education when looking at health risks?

options.A: As permanent problems that public health programs can never fix
options.B: As important warning signs to help us protect vulnerable people
options.C: As proof that a specific person will definitely commit a crime
options.D: As minor issues that have no real effect on mental health

explanation: Great thinking! Understanding these root causes helps nurses and public health teams focus their support where it's needed most.

question: Which of these is NOT a good public health strategy for controlling parasite infections?

options.A: Treating community populations with deworming drugs
options.B: Promoting open-air defecation near water sources
options.C: Ensuring access to safe and clean drinking water
options.D: Improving sanitation infrastructure and sewage systems

explanation: Open-air defecation near water sources actually spreads parasite eggs and worsens outbreaks—definitely a practice we want to stop! You got this.

question: Why do modern healthcare facilities promote a blame-free reporting culture for medication errors?

options.A: It encourages open reporting to identify system flaws and prevent future errors
options.B: It reduces the need for expensive hospital legal representation
options.C: It ensures that nurses never have to face consequences for careless mistakes
options.D: It speeds up the process of discharging patients from the hospital

explanation: When staff feel safe from unfair punishment, they report mistakes honestly, allowing the team to fix underlying system weaknesses. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h8)

question: Which nursing action is most helpful for catching fluid balance problems early in patients at risk for Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: Restricting all oral fluids
options.B: Checking blood pressure twice a week
options.C: Weighing the patient once a month
options.D: Tracking daily intake and output

explanation: Strict monitoring of fluid input and output helps nurses evaluate kidney function and hydration status during high-risk treatment periods. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h5)

question: What should you do FIRST when a portable monitor suddenly lets out a loud, urgent alarm?

options.A: Document a cardiac arrest in the patient chart right away
options.B: Immediately silence the device and walk away to find a doctor
options.C: Turn off the monitor power switch to stop the annoying noise
options.D: Assess the patient's physical condition and check the sensor placement

explanation: Patient first, always! Check the patient and make sure the sensor hasn't just popped off before jumping to conclusions.

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before encouraging a patient to take high-dose supplements?

options.A: To find out if the patient is allergic to plastic medicine bottles
options.B: To make sure the patient can afford the expensive brand names sold in pharmacies
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bed tax for nutritional therapy
options.D: To confirm the specific nutrient deficiency rather than guessing based on general fatigue

explanation: We test to be sure what's actually lacking. Guessing can lead to wasting money or even vitamin toxicity!

question: What is the main reason we put erythromycin eye ointment in a newborn's eyes?

options.A: To lubricate dry corneas caused by bright delivery lights
options.B: To reduce swelling of the eyelids from fluid retention
options.C: To treat an active bacterial sinus infection
options.D: To prevent blindness from maternal sexually transmitted infections

explanation: This simple ointment protects the baby's eyes from infections like gonorrhoea or chlamydia they might pick up while passing through the birth canal.

question: What makes a longitudinal research design special?

options.A: Collecting data from the same participants repeatedly over time
options.B: Testing a new drug without telling the patients
options.C: Comparing two different hospitals during the same month
options.D: Surveying a large group of patients just once

explanation: Spot on! Longitudinal studies are great because they follow the exact same group of people and measure things on multiple occasions to see how they change.

question: A patient with a challenging personality tries to manipulate the nursing staff by asking different nurses for special rules. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Ignore the patient completely and refuse to answer any of their call lights
options.B: Scold the patient publicly so they feel embarrassed and stop asking
options.C: Let the patient break the rules to keep them happy and prevent arguments
options.D: Ensure all staff members consistently communicate and enforce the same unit boundaries

explanation: Consistency among all staff members prevents manipulation and helps patients learn reliable, healthy boundaries. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the safest way to carry a full medical waste bag?

options.A: Drag it across the floor to avoid straining your back muscles
options.B: Hug it tightly against the chest to balance the heavy weight
options.C: Lift it by the neck and keep it away from the body
options.D: Balance it on the shoulder while walking to the disposal site

explanation: Hold the bag by its neck away from your body. That way, if a hidden needle pokes through the plastic, it won't hit you!

question: When drafting questions for an interview guide, which type of question should you definitely avoid?

options.A: Open-ended questions
options.B: Broad introductory questions
options.C: Clear and simple questions
options.D: Leading questions

explanation: Well done! Leading questions secretly push the patient toward a specific answer (like 'You take your drugs on time, right?'). We want honest, unbiased stories!

question: What is the most important step for controlling a waterborne reservoir like cholera?

options.A: Distributing insect repellant sprays to families
options.B: Administering topical skin ointments to citizens
options.C: Purifying and treating public water supplies
options.D: Isolating pet cats and dogs in urban centers

explanation: Since cholera germs love hanging out in water, cleaning up and treating public water supplies directly cuts off the source of the outbreak.

question: Why is allowing periods of silence during a palliative nursing conversation beneficial?

options.A: It forces the patient to speak up faster
options.B: It gives the patient time to gather thoughts and process heavy emotions
options.C: It allows the nurse to complete charting without talking
options.D: It shows the nurse has run out of medical information to share

explanation: Silence creates a safe, unhurried space for vulnerable patients to process profound thoughts and feelings. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h5)

question: How does naloxone successfully reverse an opioid overdose?

options.A: It binds competitively to opioid receptors, displacing the narcotic drug.
options.B: It coats the gastric lining to prevent further absorption of pills.
options.C: It stimulates liver enzymes to break down heroin into inactive metabolites.
options.D: It directly paralyzes respiratory muscles to force a regular breathing rhythm.

explanation: Naloxone has a stronger attraction (affinity) for opioid receptors than the narcotic drug itself. It swoops in, kicks the opioid off the receptor, and wakes up the patient's breathing!

question: What does the vital infection control rule 'one needle, one syringe, one time' mean for your daily practice?

options.A: Injection equipment must be used for only one patient and never reused
options.B: Syringes can be reused if they are washed with soap and water
options.C: Multiple patients can share a medication vial if a new needle is attached
options.D: Nurses should change needles between patients but keep the same syringe

explanation: It's simple and non-negotiable: a fresh, sterile needle and syringe for every single patient, every single time. You've got this rule down!

question: In simple terms, what is a research hypothesis?

options.A: A tentative prediction about the study variables
options.B: A summary of financial costs for the project
options.C: A proven fact gathered from historical records
options.D: A list of equipment needed for data collection

explanation: A hypothesis is basically your educated guess about what you think your study will discover. You test it to see if you're right!

question: What is a common clinical consequence for nurses when the health sector is chronically underfunded?

options.A: Higher salaries and improved workplace safety standards
options.B: An abundance of modern diagnostic equipment on every ward
options.C: Decreased patient wait times in accident and emergency units
options.D: Severe burnout from heavy patient-to-staff ratios

explanation: Underfunding means fewer staff and fewer resources, leaving the nurses on duty to handle overwhelming patient crowds. Burnout is a very real challenge here!

question: When should you refer a reproductive health patient to a specialist counselor?

options.A: When emotional distress exceeds basic supportive nursing care
options.B: Whenever the patient asks what medication they are taking
options.C: Only after the patient has completed all surgical treatments
options.D: Before the nurse performs any physical assessment

explanation: Spot on! While you provide great initial comfort, deep or complex emotional distress is best handled by mental health specialists.

question: A patient is treated for scabies in your clinic. What must you tell them about the rest of people living in their house?

options.A: Family members should take oral antibiotics to prevent secondary boils
options.B: Household members only need treatment if they sleep in the same bed
options.C: Only family members who are scratching should visit the clinic for cream
options.D: All household contacts must be treated at the same time, regardless of symptoms

explanation: You've got it! Because scabies spreads before itching starts, treating everyone under the roof at the same time is the only way to kick it out for good.

question: Why is pre-contraception counseling so important in family planning clinics?

options.A: It is legally required before a patient can purchase over-the-counter condoms
options.B: It permanently prevents users from ever changing their chosen method
options.C: It helps clients choose a method that suits their lifestyle while addressing fears or myths
options.D: It replaces the need for any physical health assessment by a doctor

explanation: You nailed it! Good counseling clears up rumors about side effects and helps clients find the contraceptive method that best fits their personal life.

question: What is raw data in a hospital setting?

options.A: Finalized hospital financial reports submitted to management
options.B: Unorganized facts and figures collected from clinical observations
options.C: Published research articles found in international medical journals
options.D: Personal opinions shared by senior nurses during ward handovers

explanation: Think of raw data as the raw ingredients! It's just the basic facts and figures gathered straight from the ward before anyone sorts or analyzes them. You've got this!

question: In polyvalent nursing, what does giving 'holistic care' mean?

options.A: Focusing strictly on medication administration schedules
options.B: Prioritizing hospital administrative rules over patients
options.C: Treating only the specific disease diagnosed by a doctor
options.D: Looking at the whole person including body and mind

explanation: Exactly! Holistic care means looking at the patient as a complete human being—body, mind, and spirit—rather than just focusing on a single symptom.

question: Why is it important for nurses to distinguish special cause variation from common cause variation?

options.A: To eliminate all types of patient illness completely
options.B: To avoid overreacting to normal daily fluctuations
options.C: To reduce the number of required nursing shifts
options.D: To ensure that nurses receive larger monthly salaries

explanation: Recognizing common cause prevents staff from chasing random noise, letting them focus their energy on true special cause changes. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h4)

question: What do we call the active, moving tip of a growing nerve fiber that navigates to its target?

options.A: Myelin sheath
options.B: Growth cone
options.C: Dendritic spine
options.D: Synaptic cleft

explanation: Spot on! The growth cone acts like a little explorer, reading chemical signals to guide the nerve fiber to its correct destination.

question: Which space contains the flowing cerebrospinal fluid that cushions your brain?

options.A: Epidural space
options.B: Subarachnoid space
options.C: Subdural space
options.D: Periosteal space

explanation: Brilliant! Cerebrospinal fluid circulates right through the subarachnoid space, giving your central nervous system a gentle, protective water bath.

question: What is the main job of the methodology section in a research proposal?

options.A: To list every book ever written on nursing
options.B: To praise previous researchers in the field
options.C: To prove that the researcher has a large budget
options.D: To explain how the study will be carried out

explanation: The methodology is your step-by-step game plan. It explains the exact tools, steps, and designs you will use to gather and check your data.

question: What is the main job of a nursing unit manager?

options.A: Handling only the financial accounts of the hospital
options.B: Balancing bedside clinical care with administrative duties
options.C: Writing national health policies for the ministry
options.D: Performing all surgical procedures in the ward

explanation: You've got this! A unit manager wears two caps: they keep an eye on patient care at the bedside while also managing the paperwork and admin tasks that keep the ward running.

question: What is the best way for nurse leaders to reduce resistance when bringing in a new workflow?

options.A: Ignoring complaints until staff members get tired of talking
options.B: Involving frontline staff in designing and testing the change
options.C: Threatening disciplinary action for anyone who asks questions
options.D: Mandating compliance immediately without any explanation or training

explanation: When nurses are part of building and testing a new idea from the start, they feel ownership and are happy to make it work!

question: A community health nurse is planning care in a village near a fast-flowing river. Which action best supports primary prevention?

options.A: Isolating infected patients in hospital wards for six months
options.B: Administering daily eye drops to every school-aged child
options.C: Educating residents on wearing protective clothing and using ivermectin
options.D: Surgically removing all subcutaneous nodules from every villager

explanation: Teaching folks how to avoid blackfly bites and combining that with community ivermectin distribution is the gold standard in public health nursing.

question: What does a p-value less than 0.05 mean in a Chi-Square test?

options.A: The results are statistically significant
options.B: The data collection process had major errors
options.C: The null hypothesis must be completely true
options.D: The sample size was definitely too small

explanation: Awesome! A p-value under 0.05 tells us our findings are real and unlikely to have just happened by random luck.

question: Which type of joint is known for having a fluid-filled space between the bones?

options.A: Fibrous joint
options.B: Suture joint
options.C: Cartilaginous joint
options.D: Synovial joint

explanation: Well done! Synovial joints are special because they have a fluid-filled cavity that keeps the bone surfaces separated and moving smoothly.

question: You are getting a trauma patient ready for an ambulance ride. What must you check and do FIRST?

options.A: Notifying the receiving physician of the patient's insurance status
options.B: Completing the detailed nursing admission notes
options.C: Washing and dressing all minor abrasions
options.D: Securing an open airway and controlling severe bleeding

explanation: Well done! Life-saving care always comes before paperwork or minor cuts. ABC comes first!

question: Why is the formulary tied closely to the National Essential Medicines List?

options.A: It replaces the need for nurses to study pharmacology in school
options.B: It ensures hospitals stock medicines needed for the most common illnesses
options.C: It forces pharmaceutical companies to stop importing foreign products
options.D: It guarantees that every citizen receives free treatment at clinics

explanation: Spot on! Linking them makes sure hospitals focus on stocking the drugs our patients need most, like treatments for malaria and common infections.

question: According to safety science, what is usually at the root of most medical errors in hospitals?

options.A: They are completely unavoidable in modern hospitals.
options.B: They occur only in surgical departments.
options.C: They are caused entirely by careless staff members.
options.D: They usually stem from complex system failures.

explanation: Modern safety studies show that errors happen because work processes or systems are flawed—not just because someone was careless. We fix systems to help nurses succeed!

question: What does patient acuity measure in workforce planning?

options.A: How sick patients are and how much care they need
options.B: How long a patient stays admitted on the ward
options.C: The total number of beds available in the hospital
options.D: The financial cost of medications given to patients

explanation: Acuity looks at illness severity to decide how many nursing hours a patient actually requires. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h2)

question: How do case studies mainly help nursing students build real-world competence?

options.A: By teaching them how to repair broken hospital equipment
options.B: By replacing all hospital ward practicals with computer games
options.C: By forcing them to memorize long lists of medical terminology
options.D: By challenging them to analyze real patient situations and plan care

explanation: Case studies bridge that gap between boring textbook theory and the actual ward by letting you think through real patient scenarios.

question: Which agency leads public health disease control and surveillance right here in Nigeria?

options.A: Standards Organisation of Nigeria
options.B: Federal Ministry of Education
options.C: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control
options.D: National Union of Road Transport Workers

explanation: Well done! The NCDC is our national public health body that takes charge of tracking outbreaks and keeping us prepared.

question: What is the recommended minimum birth spacing interval to protect maternal and child health?

options.A: One year apart
options.B: Exactly five years apart
options.C: Six months apart
options.D: Two to three years apart

explanation: Waiting two to three years between pregnancies allows the mother's body to recover fully and reduces risks for the newborn. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is the biopsychosocial model especially useful in psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It helps nurses look at the whole person rather than just one symptom
options.B: It ensures that every patient receives the exact same treatment plan
options.C: It replaces the need for any laboratory testing or physical exams
options.D: It proves that all mental illnesses are caused by bad parenting

explanation: Because mental disorders have multiple roots, this model encourages nurses to assess physical, emotional, and social aspects of a patient's life for holistic care. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h1)

question: You find an adult collapsed on the floor, gasping occasionally and not responding when you call them. What should you do first?

options.A: Check the blood pressure using a manual sphygmomanometer
options.B: Administer oral glucose assuming a diabetic emergency
options.C: Confirm unresponsiveness and prepare to use an AED
options.D: Wait ten minutes to see if normal breathing returns

explanation: That irregular gasping is called agonal breathing—it's a sign of cardiac arrest! Act fast, confirm they're unresponsive, and get your emergency response started.

question: What is the main goal of fire safety when you are caring for a patient in their home?

options.A: Installing hospital-grade sprinkler systems in every room
options.B: Replacing all home appliances with new models
options.C: Proactive risk reduction to protect clients and nurses
options.D: Eliminating the need for local fire departments

explanation: Spotting dangers early is key! Home fire safety is all about stopping fires before they even start so everyone stays safe.

question: What is the name of the serious pocket of pus that can form in the ovary and tube during a severe infection?

options.A: Cervical fibroid
options.B: Vicular cyst
options.C: Tubo-ovarian abscess
options.D: Endometrial polyp

explanation: When a severe infection goes unchecked, it can form a pus-filled pocket called a tubo-ovarian abscess. It's a key complication every nurse should watch out for.

question: Which global agency is best known for rushing emergency food relief to disaster zones?

options.A: International Red Cross
options.B: World Health Organization
options.C: World Food Programme
options.D: Doctors Without Borders

explanation: The World Food Programme (WFP) is the main UN body fighting global hunger, famous for getting food trucks and aid into crisis areas quickly.

question: Which of these substances should you NEVER use to soothe dry nostrils during oxygen therapy because of fire risks?

options.A: Petroleum jelly
options.B: Aqueous cream
options.C: Water-based gel
options.D: Saline nasal spray

explanation: Never use petroleum-based products around oxygen! They are flammable and can easily catch fire in an oxygen-rich environment—always stick to water-based options.

question: Which of these should normally NOT slip through the kidney's filter into your urine?

options.A: Sodium mineral ions
options.B: Filtered water molecules
options.C: Large plasma proteins
options.D: Dissolved glucose molecules

explanation: Correct! A healthy kidney filter has tiny pores that keep big things like proteins and blood cells safely inside your bloodstream.

question: You notice a yellow infectious waste bag is overflowing on your treatment trolley. What should you do?

options.A: Leave the bag open until the end of the shift for the cleaning crew
options.B: Tie the bag securely and replace it with a new one without pressing the contents down
options.C: Press the waste down firmly with both hands to make room for more items
options.D: Transfer some of the infectious waste into the general office dustbin

explanation: Never push down on a waste bag with your hands! Hidden needles or sharp bits can easily pierce the bag and give you a severe injury.

question: Why is it so important to use a client-centered approach during family planning counseling?

options.A: It allows the nurse to choose the most expensive method available
options.B: It stops the client from asking questions about side effects
options.C: It guarantees that the client will choose permanent sterilization
options.D: It ensures the client selects a method that fits her lifestyle and health needs

explanation: Nursing is all about the patient! When a client helps choose her own method, she feels respected and is much more likely to use it correctly.

question: What is the main cause of Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Gradual resistance of body cells to normal insulin
options.C: Temporary hormone changes during pregnancy
options.D: Poor dietary intake of refined carbohydrates

explanation: In Type 1 diabetes, the body's immune system gets confused and mistakenly attacks the insulin-making beta cells in the pancreas. Brilliant to keep this distinction in mind!

question: As a nurse, which group of bloodborne germs do you need to watch out for most when dealing with infectious waste?

options.A: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV
options.B: Staphylococcus and streptococcus
options.C: Malaria parasites and yellow fever
options.D: Tuberculosis, cholera, and typhoid

explanation: These three bloodborne viruses are our biggest worry in the ward because they are easily spread through accidental needle pricks and carry serious long-term health risks.

question: When are helicopter or boat transport methods most necessary during a disaster evacuation?

options.A: When floods, landslides, or collapsed bridges block traditional roads
options.B: When the patient has a minor injury and lives next to a hospital
options.C: When hospital emergency rooms are completely empty
options.D: When ground ambulances are running low on diesel fuel only

explanation: Spot on! When roads are completely impassable due to natural disasters, air and water transport are the only ways out.

question: A patient runs out of insulin two weeks after a storm destroys nearby pharmacies. What type of disaster impact is this?

options.A: Technological impact
options.B: Acute biological impact
options.C: Indirect impact
options.D: Direct impact

explanation: When health problems pop up later because medical supplies got cut off, we call that an indirect impact. Every question you try makes you a better nurse!

question: When a yellow fever patient enters the dangerous intoxication phase, which organs take the hardest hit?

options.A: Skin and joints
options.B: Liver and kidneys
options.C: Lungs and brain
options.D: Heart and pancreas

explanation: Well done! This severe stage targets vital internal organs, especially the liver (causing the yellow eyes) and the kidneys. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h3)

question: How does low health awareness usually affect when people go to the hospital?

options.A: It often delays people from seeking care until their sickness gets really bad
options.B: It makes them rush in immediately for minor surgeries
options.C: It forces patients to only use expensive private hospitals
options.D: It stops communities from needing health education entirely

explanation: Exactly. When people don't recognize early signs of illness, they often stay at home or use local herbs, only visiting the clinic when things turn into an emergency.

question: What do we call the inner struggle a person feels regarding their beliefs or connection to the sacred?

options.A: Somatic disorder
options.B: Sensory overload
options.C: Cognitive fatigue
options.D: Spiritual distress

explanation: Spiritual distress happens when someone goes through a deep crisis that shakes their faith, beliefs, or sense of purpose. Spotting this helps us support them better.

question: What physical sign strongly suggests a wound is developing a local bacterial infection?

options.A: Clear, watery fluid leaking in small amounts
options.B: Purulent drainage and surrounding redness
options.C: Rapid tightening of the surrounding scar tissue
options.D: Cool skin temperature around the dressing edges

explanation: Pus and redness are classic signs that white blood cells are fighting a heavy bacterial invasion in the tissue. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the function of the one-way valves inside medium veins?

options.A: Filter bacteria out of returning blood
options.B: Add oxygen back into venous blood
options.C: Regulate body temperature in limbs
options.D: Prevent blood from flowing backward

explanation: Venous valves ensure that blood moves in only one direction—toward the heart—against the pull of gravity. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h5)

question: Where in the brain is the main control center that keeps your breathing rhythm on autopilot?

options.A: Hypothalamus and pituitary gland
options.B: Medulla oblongata and pons
options.C: Cerebrum and cerebral cortex
options.D: Cerebellum and spinal cord

explanation: Correct! The brainstem quietly manages your breathing rhythm in the background so you don't have to think about it.

question: What is pica, a condition nurses watch out for during dietary checks?

options.A: An allergic reaction to eating citrus fruits during pregnancy
options.B: An excessive thirst that leads to drinking too much water daily
options.C: A complete loss of appetite caused by severe hormonal changes
options.D: A strong craving to eat non-food items like clay, starch, or ice

explanation: Pica happens when a mum craves non-food items like chalk or clay. It's usually the body's way of whispering that she lacks certain minerals like iron!

question: Why is it super important to check if a research study is valid before using its findings on your hospital ward?

options.A: To make sure nurses get extra credit for reading
options.B: To make sure the hospital buys the newest equipment
options.C: To prevent using flawed ideas that could harm patients
options.D: To save money on printing out research papers

explanation: As future nurses, our top priority is patient safety. If research is flawed, applying it on the ward could lead to poor patient care.

question: When a doctor prescribes medication for a child's conduct disorder, what is the main purpose?

options.A: Permanently curing the underlying behaviour disorder
options.B: Targeting specific symptoms like severe aggression or hyperactivity
options.C: Replacing the need for any behavioral therapy
options.D: Ensuring the child gets higher grades in school

explanation: Medications are used alongside therapy to control tough, disruptive symptoms—they aren't a standalone cure, but they offer great relief.

question: Why is forcing an exhausted nurse to work a double shift an ethical and legal concern?

options.A: It reduces the amount of paperwork filed in the office
options.B: It always results in immediate promotion for the nurse
options.C: It increases the risk of medical errors and patient harm
options.D: It breaks hospital rules regarding uniform colors

explanation: Exhausted nurses are more prone to mistakes, which threatens patient safety and opens the facility to liability. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h8)

question: Why can a PET scan often detect diseases earlier than other imaging methods?

options.A: It uses a much higher radiation dose than standard diagnostic tests.
options.B: It spots abnormal chemical changes in cells before physical damage occurs.
options.C: It relies on the body's natural magnetic field rather than external machines.
options.D: It examines every single organ in the human body simultaneously.

explanation: Spot on! Cells change how they behave and use energy long before an organ shows visible damage on a regular X-ray or CT scan, letting PET catch problems early.

question: Why is overfilling a sharps safety box a dangerous hazard?

options.A: It prevents the incineration machine from burning paper waste
options.B: It increases the chemical weight of the plastic container
options.C: It automatically dissolves the cardboard exterior
options.D: It exposes handlers and cleaners to protruding needles

explanation: Overfilled boxes mean needles are sticking out, ready to accidentally prick anyone who handles or carries them. Close and replace those boxes before they get too full!

question: A community health nurse wants to help reduce FGM rates in a rural village. Which strategy works best for lasting change?

options.A: Ignoring the practice to avoid offending cultural traditions
options.B: Performing mild pricks in the clinic to keep traditions alive safely
options.C: Engaging local leaders and educators in discussions about health risks
options.D: Arresting every mother without talking to the community

explanation: Brilliant! Real, lasting change happens when you work hand-in-hand with the community to shift mindsets and choose health together.

question: Why must nurses keep reassessing patients who have already been sorted into a triage category?

options.A: Rescue teams need to change patient names frequently
options.B: Color tags often fall off in wet weather conditions
options.C: Hospital admission clerks require updated paperwork every hour
options.D: A patient's condition can rapidly deteriorate over time

explanation: Exactly! Injuries can hide beneath the surface, meaning a patient who looks stable now could crash and need urgent help a few minutes later.

question: What must a nurse do before changing how they care for patients based on a new research paper?

options.A: Carefully check the study's validity and methods first
options.B: Wait ten whole years before taking any action
options.C: Just assume it's true because it was printed in a magazine
options.D: Ask every single hospital patient for their permission

explanation: Evidence-based practice means we don't just follow every new trend blindly; we appraise the research to make sure it's solid and safe.

question: Roughly what percentage of waste coming out of a healthcare facility is actually considered hazardous?

options.A: 75 to 90 percent
options.B: 10 to 25 percent
options.C: 50 to 60 percent
options.D: 95 to 99 percent

explanation: Most hospital waste is regular everyday trash (like office paper and food wrappers). Only about 10 to 25 percent is truly hazardous and needs special handling. You've got this!

question: What is the best way for a nurse to provide psychological first aid to a disaster victim?

options.A: Encouraging the victim to forget the event and focus on rebuilding
options.B: Offering a calm presence and active listening without false promises
options.C: Leaving the victim alone immediately so they can process their grief
options.D: Telling the victim that everything will quickly return to normal

explanation: Wonderful! Psychological first aid is all about being present, listening patiently, and supporting them without making promises you can't keep.

question: Which of the following statements about legally blind individuals is true?

options.A: Most retain some form of residual vision or light perception
options.B: They cannot hear or speak normally compared to others
options.C: They experience total pitch darkness without any exceptions
options.D: Their condition can always be cured with minor surgery

explanation: Legal blindness is a definition for benefits and care, but very few people with this status see absolute blackness; most have usable light or shape awareness. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why do many health workers hesitate to take up jobs in poor rural areas?

options.A: Medical equipment cannot function without advanced urban laboratory setups
options.B: Government policies forbid deploying trained professionals outside state capitals
options.C: Workers are reluctant to live in areas lacking basic infrastructure and security
options.D: Rural residents refuse to seek care from qualified nurses and midwives

explanation: Everyone wants a safe home, electricity, good schools for their kids, and basic amenities. Without these, rural postings are a hard sell.

question: What is the main difference between tele-health and tele-medicine?

options.A: Tele-medicine includes nursing care while tele-health does not.
options.B: Tele-health is strictly used for emergency surgical procedures.
options.C: Tele-health covers a broader range of services including education and administration.
options.D: Tele-medicine relies on traditional mail rather than electronic devices.

explanation: Think of tele-health as the big umbrella that covers all health services—like patient education and admin work—while tele-medicine focuses specifically on medical diagnosis and treatment.

question: A community health nurse notices many teens in her local area know nothing about birth control. What is her best first step?

options.A: Report all teenagers to the local police division for investigation
options.B: Establish an educational youth-friendly reproductive health club at the local center
options.C: Wait until patients present with complications before offering advice
options.D: Ban all public discussions regarding sexual health in schools

explanation: Creating safe, welcoming spaces gives adolescents the accurate facts they need to protect their health and futures. Great nursing initiative!

question: A staff nurse administers the wrong IV fluid, injuring a patient while on duty in a public hospital. Who can be sued alongside the nurse?

options.A: The patient's next of kin
options.B: The hospital management or employing authority
options.C: The Nursing and Midwifery Council registrar
options.D: The pharmaceutical manufacturing company

explanation: Because the nurse was doing their job at the time, the hospital shares the responsibility under the rule of vicarious liability. Teamwork means shared accountability!

question: How do digital tracking dashboards help nurses working in a Rapid Response Center?

options.A: By providing real-time data on regional hospital bed availability and patient status
options.B: By replacing all face-to-face communication between medical staff
options.C: By predicting future natural disasters days before they happen
options.D: By automatically treating patient wounds without human intervention

explanation: Dashboards give coordinators an instant view of open hospital beds so they know exactly where to send incoming patients.

question: What is the main job of the accessory (helper) female reproductive organs?

options.A: To support fertilization, gestation, and childbirth
options.B: To produce female hormones and mature eggs
options.C: To filter toxins from the pelvic blood supply
options.D: To regulate the monthly menstrual bleeding cycle

explanation: You got it! While ovaries make the eggs, the accessory organs provide the pathways, protection, and home for a baby to grow.

question: What does an Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) blood test look for?

options.A: The amount of oxygen bound to hemoglobin
options.B: The total number of red blood cells in circulation
options.C: The presence of bacterial pathogens in the bloodstream
options.D: The presence of antibodies that attack the body's own cell nuclei

explanation: An ANA test checks for rogue antibodies that target the control center (nucleus) of our cells, which helps doctors spot systemic autoimmune issues.

question: What type of pen ink is recommended for writing in manual health records to ensure longevity?

options.A: Washable water-based ink
options.B: Pencil for easy erasing
options.C: Red ink for all entries
options.D: Permanent black or blue ink

explanation: Permanent ink ensures that records do not fade, smudge with humidity, or get easily altered over time. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h7)

question: What goes wrong when a manager only treats the surface symptoms of a ward problem?

options.A: Hospital management will immediately fire the nursing staff
options.B: The budget for the ward will be permanently frozen
options.C: The underlying issue remains and will happen again
options.D: Patients will stop coming to the clinic entirely

explanation: Just scratching the surface leaves the root cause untouched. Until you fix the core issue, the exact same problem is bound to return.

question: Once breastfeeding is well established (Lactogenesis III), how does the body keep making enough milk?

options.A: By continuous hormonal signals sent from the anterior pituitary gland
options.B: By the structural expansion of the lobulo-alveolar system
options.C: By high circulating levels of progesterone stored in adipose tissue
options.D: By an autocrine supply-and-demand mechanism based on milk removal

explanation: It's all about supply and demand! The more the baby feeds and empties the breast, the more milk your body gets the signal to make.

question: What is the statistical word for the value that shows up most often in a set of data?

options.A: Range
options.B: Mean
options.C: Median
options.D: Mode

explanation: You got it! Just remember: **Mo**de is the value that appears **mo**st often. Easy peasy!

question: A resident says they feel unsteady walking to the dining hall. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Assess their footwear, use of assistive devices, and recent medications
options.B: Scold the resident for walking without supervision
options.C: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent bathroom trips
options.D: Advise the resident to stay permanently in bed for safety

explanation: Finding the exact cause—like bad shoes, a missing walking stick, or a dizzying drug side effect—helps fix the problem at the root. Spot on!

question: What is the primary reason governments get involved in the food supply?

options.A: To set the exact menu for every household
options.B: To protect public health and ensure stability
options.C: To control all farming businesses in the country
options.D: To eliminate the need for private grocery stores

explanation: Governments intervene primarily to safeguard the health and well-being of the population through safe and stable food systems. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h1)

question: Why should nursing schools include hands-on mini-projects during training?

options.A: It provides free labor for hospital administrative departments
options.B: It stops students from pursuing bedside clinical nursing careers
options.C: It builds confidence and practical skills in carrying out future studies
options.D: It ensures students pass their board exams without studying textbooks

explanation: Exactly! Doing small projects early on takes away the anxiety so you feel like a capable researcher long before you graduate.

question: A pregnant woman experiences chronic malnutrition late in pregnancy. Which nutrient transfer process is most likely to be affected first regarding fetal bone development?

options.A: Pinocytosis of maternal immunoglobulins
options.B: Active transport of minerals like calcium
options.C: Simple diffusion of respiratory oxygen
options.D: Facilitated diffusion of free water

explanation: Minerals like calcium require active transport mechanisms powered by energy to build up in the fetal skeleton, which can be strained under severe maternal nutritional deficits. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h5)

question: Why is patient education important before discharge on a modified diet?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never need dental work again
options.B: It stops the patient from ever eating solid food
options.C: It helps family members prepare safe food textures at home
options.D: It replaces the need for follow-up doctor appointments

explanation: Educating patients and caregivers ensures they continue safe food preparation and know what to avoid after leaving the hospital. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h8)

question: How does a pregnant woman's total blood volume usually change during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: It decreases sharply to prevent high blood pressure.
options.B: It remains completely unchanged throughout gestation.
options.C: It increases by nearly half to support the placenta.
options.D: It fluctuates wildly based on daily fluid intake.

explanation: Amazing body fact: a mum's blood volume expands by almost 50% to make sure the baby and placenta get all the blood and oxygen they need!

question: You feel a patient's uterus (fundus) on her second day after birth and notice it feels soft and is higher than expected. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward
options.B: Massage the fundus gently until it becomes firm
options.C: Administer an intravenous fluid bolus
options.D: Document that the uterus is healing normally

explanation: A soft or 'boggy' uterus needs a little help! Massaging it gently makes the muscle fibers tighten up, which stops heavy bleeding. You're doing great.

question: Where do community health nurses usually first notice unusual patterns of disease?

options.A: During routine home visits, school check-ups, or clinic duties
options.B: While managing hospital kitchen menus and supply inventories
options.C: During international travel conferences held in capital cities
options.D: While reviewing global financial market reports in an office

explanation: Nurses encounter patients directly in communities and clinics, making them the primary observers of local health changes. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h6)

question: Apart from bedside clinical work, what is a key role for a community health nurse?

options.A: Purchasing medical equipment for tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: Financing the construction of primary healthcare centers
options.C: Acting as an educator and facilitator for health programs
options.D: Drafting national health policies in the federal ministry

explanation: You nailed it! Community nurses spend a lot of time teaching families, running workshops, and helping communities organize their own health activities.

question: Which test gives the final confirmation that a patient has active lung TB?

options.A: Physical auscultation of bilateral lung sounds
options.B: Routine complete blood count and electrolyte panel
options.C: Measurement of resting blood pressure and pulse rate
options.D: Sputum culture and acid-fast bacilli smear testing

explanation: Checking the patient's sputum for acid-fast bacilli or growing the germs in a lab gives the definitive proof needed to confirm active TB.

question: Why are anti-nausea meds usually given before chemo starts instead of waiting for nausea to begin?

options.A: Preventing nausea before it starts is much more effective than treating it later
options.B: They help the patient fall asleep during the long infusion
options.C: Chemotherapy drugs will not dissolve properly without them
options.D: They taste better when taken on an empty stomach

explanation: Prevention is key! Giving these meds early blocks the vomiting center before chemo triggers it. Brilliant clinical thinking!

question: A patient with a severe head injury has a total GCS score of 7. What does this score tell you about their safety?

options.A: The patient is ready for discharge to home care.
options.B: The patient is fully conscious and oriented.
options.C: The patient likely needs advanced airway protection and close monitoring.
options.D: The patient has mild confusion and will recover quickly without intervention.

explanation: Any GCS score of 8 or lower means serious trouble. The patient usually can't protect their own airway and needs close watch or intubation.

question: Why does the Model for Improvement focus on small tests of change rather than massive overhauls?

options.A: Hospital management bans large projects due to budget constraints
options.B: Small tests reduce risk and let staff see if a change works before spreading it
options.C: Regulatory bodies only permit one minor change per year
options.D: Patients refuse to participate in large-scale hospital studies

explanation: Spot on! Testing things on a small scale lets nurses safely try out new ideas without disrupting the whole ward.

question: What does scientific empiricism primarily rely on for gathering medical knowledge?

options.A: Strict adherence to ancient religious texts
options.B: Careful observation and physical experimentation
options.C: Interpreting dreams and spiritual visions
options.D: Blind trust in traditional folklore

explanation: Empiricism values tangible evidence gained through direct observation, testing, and experimentation rather than accepting claims based on tradition or authority alone. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why does climate change present a growing challenge for modern public health nurses?

options.A: It forces all hospitals to permanently close their emergency departments
options.B: It eliminates the need for vaccines and routine community health education
options.C: It prevents nurses from traveling on paved urban highways
options.D: It drives displacement, food insecurity, and the spread of vector-borne diseases

explanation: Environmental shifts expand the reach of diseases like malaria and create widespread displacement that strains community health systems. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h9)

question: Why is solid political backing so important for keeping fake drugs out of Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: It removes the need for trained pharmacists in community clinics
options.B: It allows politicians to personally manufacture essential vaccines
options.C: It guarantees that all drugs are imported free of import duties
options.D: It enforces regulatory oversight to prevent counterfeit drugs from entering the market

explanation: Correct! Agencies like NAFDAC need strong legal backing and political support to crack down on counterfeit medications and keep patients safe.

question: What is the main difference between a delayed union and a nonunion?

options.A: Delayed union requires surgery, while nonunion heals on its own with rest.
options.B: Delayed union takes longer than normal, while nonunion fails to heal entirely.
options.C: Delayed union involves infection, while nonunion is caused by blood clots.
options.D: Delayed union happens in children, while nonunion happens only in the elderly.

explanation: Think of delayed union as a slow student who eventually finishes the exam, while nonunion means the student simply gave up and stopped trying altogether.

question: When dressing a stroke patient with weakness on one side, where should you put the clothes first?

options.A: Whichever side they prefer
options.B: The strong or unaffected side
options.C: Both sides at the exact same time
options.D: The weak or affected side

explanation: Brilliant! Dressing the weak side first saves the patient from painful, awkward twisting of a limb that lacks strength.

question: What is a common weakness faced by community-based health financing schemes in Nigeria?

options.A: Complete absence of any local healthcare facilities to utilize
options.B: Mandatory participation of international pharmaceutical conglomerates
options.C: Small risk pools and limited financial reserves during economic hardships
options.D: Excessive funding from the central government that causes inflation

explanation: Because CBHI covers smaller groups, a wave of simultaneous illnesses or economic hard times can quickly drain their funds. A great concept that still faces growth hurdles!

question: Why are unsafe injection practices such a big public health problem?

options.A: They make injectable medications completely ineffective
options.B: They increase the physical pain of receiving treatment
options.C: They rapidly spread blood-borne pathogens to large numbers of people
options.D: They cause immediate allergic reactions in all recipients

explanation: Sharing needles or contaminating medication vials can quickly transmit serious blood-borne infections across many patients in a short time. You've got this!

question: As a working nurse, why is it helpful to understand basic data processing?

options.A: To help them evaluate new hospital guidelines and clinical research
options.B: To replace hospital statisticians during busy morning shifts
options.C: To manage the hospital financial payroll system directly
options.D: To diagnose rare diseases without using laboratory tests

explanation: You don't need to be a statistician! Knowing how data turns into evidence helps you decide if a new hospital guideline is actually trustworthy for your patients.

question: What happens if a research question is unclear or confusing?

options.A: Readers and data collectors will not know what is actually being measured
options.B: The institutional review board will automatically approve it
options.C: The study will take fewer days to complete
options.D: Data analysis becomes completely unnecessary

explanation: Clarity is key. If your question is confusing, anyone helping you collect data will be lost, leading to messy results that don't make sense.

question: According to Maslow, what must be met first before a person worries about higher career goals?

options.A: Advanced leadership training courses
options.B: Basic survival and safety needs
options.C: Complete clinical independence
options.D: Personal social media recognition

explanation: Just like building a house, you need a solid foundation. Basic needs like food, rest, and safety come first before we focus on big career heights.

question: Why should a QI team share their updates with the rest of the unit staff?

options.A: To legally transfer responsibility for project failures away from nurses
options.B: To ensure administrative managers meet their annual reporting quotas
options.C: To prevent unit staff from asking questions during shift changes
options.D: To keep everyone informed and encourage buy-in for new workflows

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the wider unit in the loop prevents staff from feeling caught off guard and helps everyone support the new practices.

question: What do second-order neurons typically do in ascending sensory pathways?

options.A: They secrete neurotransmitters onto sweat glands
options.B: They directly connect skin receptors to motor neurons
options.C: They cross the midline and ascend to the thalamus
options.D: They store long-term sensory memories in the frontal lobe

explanation: You got it! Second-order neurons cross over (decussate) to the opposite side of the spinal cord or brainstem before heading up to the thalamus.

question: How do major structural uterine defects often lead to repeated miscarriages?

options.A: By permanently destroying all hormones needed to maintain a menstrual cycle
options.B: By limiting the physical space available for normal fetal growth and disrupting proper implantation
options.C: By stopping the ovaries from releasing mature eggs every month
options.D: By completely blocking blood flow to the lower extremities

explanation: That is correct! An irregular or restricted uterine cavity makes it hard for a growing embryo to implant safely and find enough room to develop.

question: What makes blunt force trauma to the abdomen so dangerous?

options.A: Permanent stiffening of the peripheral joints
options.B: Immediate infection of the superficial skin layers
options.C: Rapid development of severe seasonal allergies
options.D: Massive internal bleeding without visible external wounds

explanation: A person can look fine on the outside while bleeding heavily inside. That's why careful, hands-on nursing assessment is always key!

question: What is the surgery called when a badly damaged joint is completely replaced with an artificial one?

options.A: Arthroscopy
options.B: Arthrodesis
options.C: Osteotomy
options.D: Arthroplasty

explanation: Spot on! Arthroplasty is the medical term for joint replacement surgery using modern metal and plastic implants.

question: What does the important humanitarian principle of 'non-refoulement' mean?

options.A: Automatic granting of permanent citizenship in the host nation
options.B: The legal right to free higher education in the host country
options.C: Protection from being forced to return to a dangerous country
options.D: Exemption from all local taxes and immigration fees

explanation: Non-refoulement is a fancy word with a vital meaning. It simply protects refugees from being sent back to places where they face serious harm or persecution.

question: What is the main purpose of formative evaluation?

options.A: To give ongoing feedback to help you learn better
options.B: To check the school's financial budget
options.C: To pass the national licensing exam
options.D: To decide your final GPA for graduation

explanation: Formative evaluation is your friendly guide while you are still learning—it gives you feedback so you can improve before any big stakes exam.

question: Why is propylthiouracil (PTU) preferred over methimazole during early pregnancy?

options.A: Methimazole is linked to specific birth defects during early pregnancy
options.B: PTU crosses the human placenta much faster than methimazole
options.C: PTU stays active in pregnant women for up to one full week
options.D: Methimazole stimulates uterine contractions and causes early labor

explanation: We avoid methimazole in the first trimester because it carries a risk of birth defects, making PTU the safer choice for mum and baby.

question: Why do we need clear, agreed-upon definitions when collecting data for quality improvement?

options.A: To ensure everyone interprets and measures terms in the exact same way
options.B: To make the research paper long enough for publication
options.C: To increase the financial budget allocated to the nursing unit
options.D: To prove that nurses are working faster than doctors

explanation: Clear definitions mean everyone is speaking the same language, so the data we collect across different shifts is reliable and true.

question: Which action shows safe, ethical nursing practice regarding alternative treatments?

options.A: Prescribing high-dose vitamins without checking laboratory values
options.B: Evaluating scientific evidence while keeping communication open with the patient
options.C: Mocking the patient for believing in natural healing methods
options.D: Pretending alternative treatments do not exist at all

explanation: Good nursing means keeping an open, non-judgmental dialogue so patients feel safe sharing what they take, while we check the facts.

question: What crucial nursing check must be done before giving food or water to a stroke patient who might have trouble swallowing?

options.A: A check for homonymous hemianopsia
options.B: A measurement of 24-hour urine output
options.C: A formal bedside swallow screen
options.D: A complete neurological Glasgow Coma Scale score

explanation: Correct! Swallowing difficulties (dysphagia) can easily lead to aspiration pneumonia. A bedside swallow screen keeps the patient safe before any oral intake.

question: Simply put, what is an antigen?

options.A: A protective protein made by B lymphocytes
options.B: A physical barrier found on human skin
options.C: A foreign substance that triggers an immune response
options.D: A type of white blood cell that eats bacteria

explanation: An antigen is basically any foreign tag or molecule on a germ that says 'intruder!' to your immune system, shouting for backup.

question: Which of these is a major factor that restricts healthcare supply?

options.A: Excessive amounts of idle medical equipment in storage
options.B: An absolute absence of government regulations in hospitals
options.C: Low costs associated with purchasing new pharmaceuticals
options.D: Shortages of qualified nursing workforce and clinical staff

explanation: Right! Even if a ward has empty beds, a shortage of trained nurses and doctors means the hospital cannot safely take in more patients.

question: What is the main reason nurses use a genogram?

options.A: To prescribe strong mental health drugs to relatives
options.B: To map out family relationships and health patterns across generations
options.C: To calculate the household's exact monthly salary
options.D: To check the caregiver's blood pressure

explanation: A genogram is basically a detailed family tree that helps you spot inherited health issues and relationship patterns at a single glance.

question: Why is having a clear 'case definition' so important during a disease outbreak?

options.A: It guarantees that the disease will not spread to neighboring towns.
options.B: It automatically cures the patients who fit the diagnostic description.
options.C: It prevents the government from spending money on laboratory testing.
options.D: It ensures all investigators identify and count cases using the exact same criteria.

explanation: Spot on! A clear case definition makes sure every nurse and doctor is looking for the exact same signs, preventing confusion in our records.

question: Why should a nurse avoid documenting subjective opinions like 'patient is lying about how she got these bruises' in a clinical chart?

options.A: Because patients are not allowed to read their own medical folders
options.B: Because clinical records require objective facts and direct quotes for legal validity
options.C: Because personal opinions are always illegal to write down
options.D: Because hospital management does not read nursing notes

explanation: Accurate, unbiased documentation protects the patient's legal rights and maintains professional nursing standards. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h5)

question: Why are nursing audits so important for quality assurance?

options.A: They reduce the cost of purchasing hospital medications
options.B: They help discover gaps between standard care and actual practice
options.C: They guarantee that patients will never experience complications
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for physician supervision

explanation: Spot on! By comparing what we actually do against established guidelines, audits show us clearly where our care needs a little extra boost.

question: Why do healthcare leaders in Nigeria often have to make tough choices about money and supplies?

options.A: Patients refuse to pay taxes for public health services
options.B: Medical technology changes too rapidly to keep track
options.C: International organizations dictate exact spending limits
options.D: Available financial and material resources are always limited

explanation: Since funds are never endless, leaders have to decide which urgent needs get funded first. It's a balancing act we see every day!

question: Why should you test a new idea on a small scale before launching it across the whole hospital?

options.A: It ensures that hospital management never finds out about the project
options.B: It eliminates all paperwork requirements for the nursing unit
options.C: It completely stops nurses from making any clinical errors ever again
options.D: It minimizes risk and allows staff to refine the process safely

explanation: Testing on a small scale lets you find little mistakes and fix them safely before rolling the change out to the entire hospital.

question: What is the main difference between skin traction and skeletal traction?

options.A: Skin traction requires surgical pins placed in the bone
options.B: Skeletal traction uses much lighter weights than skin traction
options.C: Skin traction uses external devices attached to the skin
options.D: Skeletal traction is only used on the upper extremities

explanation: Skin traction applies pulling force from the outside using tapes, boots, or straps, while skeletal traction uses pins or wires placed directly into the bone. You've got this!

question: Which group is most at risk for protein-energy malnutrition during the transition to family foods?

options.A: Healthy young adult athletes
options.B: Middle-aged male farmers
options.C: Infants and young children
options.D: Retired elderly office workers

explanation: Young children transitioning from breast milk or formula to family foods are at high risk if their new diet lacks sufficient nutrients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h3)

question: Why is a first-come, first-served system a bad idea in emergency room triage?

options.A: It takes too much time for computer systems to log patients in order
options.B: Patients prefer waiting longer periods for their evaluations
options.C: Hospital administrators legally forbid using arrival times for care
options.D: It could cause a critically ill patient to die in the waiting room while a minor case is seen first

explanation: Triage ensures that limited life-saving resources go straight to the sickest patients first, preventing tragic delays.

question: A nurse ignores a ward medication rule, and the patient gets hurt. What legal problem might this cause?

options.A: The hospital policy automatically protects the nurse from blame
options.B: The legal system ignores internal hospital rules completely
options.C: The policy becomes invalid because a nurse chose not to use it
options.D: The breach of policy can be used as evidence of negligence

explanation: Skipping established safety steps without a good clinical reason makes it much easier to prove a breach of duty if something goes wrong.

question: What fluid mainly fills the hollow chambers (ventricles) inside the brain?

options.A: Venous whole blood
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: Lymphatic interstitial fluid
options.D: Extracellular matrix

explanation: Great job! The brain ventricles are special hollow spaces that continuously make and store cerebrospinal fluid to keep the brain cushioned and nourished.

question: Which specific protein in the intestine makes Oral Rehydration Therapy work so well?

options.A: SGLT1
options.B: Gastric lipase
options.C: Potassium pump
options.D: Insulin receptor

explanation: SGLT1 (sodium-glucose linked transporter type 1) is the hero protein! It links sugar and salt uptake in the small intestine to pull precious water into the body.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to learning in a hospital setting?

options.A: Constant noise and staff interruptions on the ward
options.B: High levels of physical pain and anxiety
options.C: Quiet, distraction-free private recovery rooms
options.D: Language differences between nurse and patient

explanation: A quiet, private room actually makes teaching easier! Noise, pain, and language gaps are the real hurdles.

question: What happens inside the eye if the fluid drainage gets blocked while the eye keeps making more fluid?

options.A: Eye pressure goes down
options.B: The ciliary body stops working
options.C: The cornea becomes completely opaque
options.D: Eye pressure goes up

explanation: Spot on! If fluid keeps pouring in but cannot flow out, it backs up and causes the pressure inside the eye to rise.

question: During a community visit, you meet a mother of seven who looks exhausted, malnourished, and pregnant again because her husband wants a boy. What is the best way to handle this first?

options.A: Advise the mother to leave her marital home immediately that same day
options.B: Prescribe high-dose iron supplements without addressing the underlying pregnancy
options.C: Publicly reprimand the husband in front of the community assembly
options.D: Offer confidential health counseling and discuss safe birth spacing options with the mother

explanation: Offering a safe, private space to talk helps the mother explore her health choices without triggering a dangerous family fight.

question: A newly bereaved widow comes to the clinic showing deep withdrawal, sleep problems, and intense fear after going through local mourning rites. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: Acute diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: Primary angle-closure glaucoma
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: The mix of trauma, harsh rituals, and isolation can easily trigger mental health struggles like PTSD and severe depression. Being able to spot this makes you a caring nurse!

question: Which drug group tricks cancer cells by looking like normal building blocks, stopping DNA growth?

options.A: Plant alkaloids
options.B: Alkylating agents
options.C: Antitumor antibiotics
options.D: Antimetabolites

explanation: Spot on! Antimetabolites look just enough like normal cell food to fool cancer cells, stopping them from making healthy DNA.

question: Why should a nurse check the target skin area before applying a prescribed cream?

options.A: To check for signs of breakdown or unexpected infection
options.B: To measure the exact surface area in square centimeters
options.C: To test the electrical conductivity of the skin cells
options.D: To determine if the patient has a systemic fever

explanation: A quick look helps you catch any new irritation or worsening infection before adding more medicine. Patient safety first!

question: Why does nursing leadership need to carry out regular program evaluations?

options.A: It reveals if the interventions are actually improving health outcomes
options.B: It ensures that no patient ever complains about the hospital
